units.statement: IGFBP2 functions as a mechanistic intermediary in the trametinib-anlotinib synergy: combined treatment downregulates IGFBP2, and exogenous IGFBP2 reverses combination-induced suppression of invasion, viability, RTK signaling, and c-MYC levels, while IGFBP2 knockdown inhibits cell-cycle gene transcription.
source_quotes: Fig. 4 IGFBP2 contributes to the high antitumor efficacy of MEK inhibitor-trametinib and RTK inhibitor-anlotinib combination treatments.
Furthermore, the combined treatment-induced decrease in the c-MYC protein level could be rescued via the addition of exogenous IGFBP2 (Fig. 4m, n).

More importantly, the combined treatment-induced inactivation of RTK pathways (including PDGFR, FSR (FGFR), EGFR, and ERBB3) along with downstream SHP2 could be reversed upon the addition of exogenous IGFBP2 (Fig. 4o).
The addition of exogenous IGFBP2 can rejuvenate RTK inactivation induced by coinhibition of the MEK and RTK pathways.
These results suggest that the synergistic antitumor activity induced by coinhibition of the MEK and RTK pathways is mediated through a reduction in IGFBP2.

Here, we found that MEK inhibitor-trametinib treatment results in the feedback activation of multiple receptor tyrosine kinases (RTKs) and that treatment with the pan-RTK inhibitor anlotinib effectively inhibits the progression of KRAS-mutant NSCLC.

In this study, we further investigated the molecular mechanism of adaptive resistance to the MEK inhibitor trametinib in KRAS- mutant NSCLC cells and revealed that trametinib-induced multiple receptor tyrosine kinase (RTK) activation plays a key role in adaptive resistance, suggesting that coinhibition of the MEK/RTK pathways via trametinib plus anlotinib administration has potential value in the treatment of KRAS-mutant NSCLC in preclinical and clinical settings.

units.statement: In the phase I clinical trial (NCT04967079) of 33 advanced non-G12C KRAS-mutant NSCLC patients, trametinib plus anlotinib achieved an integrated ORR of 66.7%, median PFS of 10.3 months, median OS of 19.7 months, average tumor shrinkage of 34.4%, and DCR of 97%, with phase Ia ORR 69.2% (6.9-month PFS) and phase Ib ORR 65% (11.5-month PFS).
